questions.q: 月初拿到 1000 元生活费，最稳的第一步是？
questions.qEN: You get ¥1,000 for the month. What's the safest first move?
options: 先把一直想买的买了，剩下慢慢花
先分成几份：吃饭、交通、存钱
先借一部分给同学，反正会还
先不管，月底看剩多少再说
optionsEN: Buy what you've wanted, then see what's left
Split it first: food, transport, savings
Lend some to a friend, they'll pay it back
Don't plan, just see what's left at month end
questions.why: 先分好再花，钱就不容易在月中花光。这就是预算。
questions.whyEN: Split it before you spend it, and it won't vanish mid-month. That's all a budget is.

questions.q: 「先存后花」比「花剩下的再存」更容易攒下钱。
questions.qEN: "Save first, then spend" works better than "save whatever's left".
questions.why: 先把要存的钱拿出来，剩下的才是能花的。这样存钱就不靠意志力。
questions.whyEN: Take the savings out first and spend what remains. Then saving doesn't depend on willpower.

questions.q: 每天一杯 15 元的奶茶，一个月（30 天）要花多少元？
questions.qEN: A ¥15 bubble tea every day. How much is that over 30 days?
questions.why: 15 × 30 = 450。小钱天天花，一个月就是一大笔。
questions.whyEN: 15 × 30 = 450. Small amounts every day add up to a big one.

questions.qEN: In the 50/30/20 rule, what does the 20 usually stand for?
options: 娱乐
必需开支
储蓄
请客
optionsEN: Fun
Essentials
Savings
Treating friends
questions.why: 常见的简易分法：50% 必需、30% 想要、20% 储蓄。学生可以按自己的情况调整比例。
questions.whyEN: A common simple split: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings. Adjust the ratio to fit your life.

questions.q: 记账的主要目的，是证明自己没有乱花钱。
questions.qEN: The main point of tracking is to prove you didn't waste money.
questions.why: 记账是为了看清钱去了哪，下次做决定有依据，不是为了自责。
questions.whyEN: Tracking shows you where money went so your next decision is better informed. It isn't about guilt.

questions.q: 这个月预算超了 100 元，最好的做法是？
questions.qEN: You went ¥100 over budget this month. Best move?
options: 跟家长说下个月再多要 100 元
找到超在哪，下月那项少花点
反正超了，这个月干脆不管了
以后不记账了，免得看着难受
optionsEN: Ask your parents for ¥100 more
Find the overspend, trim it next month
It's blown anyway, forget this month
Stop tracking so it stops feeling bad
questions.why: 超支不可怕，找到原因、调整一项就好。预算是用来调的，不是用来考试的。
questions.whyEN: Going over isn't a disaster. Find the cause and adjust one category. A budget is meant to be tuned.

questions.q: 想买一双 600 元的球鞋，每周能存 50 元，需要几周？
questions.qEN: You want ¥600 sneakers and can save ¥50 a week. How many weeks?
questions.why: 600 ÷ 50 = 12 周。把目标拆成每周的小数目，就知道要坚持多久。
questions.whyEN: 600 ÷ 50 = 12 weeks. Breaking a goal into weekly amounts tells you how long it takes.

questions.q: 以下哪一项最适合算作「固定支出」？
questions.qEN: Which one is a fixed expense?
options: 每月手机话费
周末看电影
放学买零食
同学生日礼物
optionsEN: Monthly phone bill
Weekend movie
After-school snacks
A friend's birthday gift
questions.why: 每个月金额差不多、而且必须付的叫固定支出。做预算要先把它扣掉。
questions.whyEN: Something you pay every month for about the same amount is fixed. Take it out before planning the rest.

questions.q: 以下哪一项最接近「需要」？
questions.qEN: Which one is closest to a need?
options: 限量款盲盒
上学用的公交卡充值
游戏皮肤
今天的第三杯奶茶
optionsEN: A limited-edition blind box
Topping up your bus card for school
A game skin
Your third bubble tea today
questions.why: 没有它会影响上学和正常生活的，才算需要。
questions.whyEN: A need is something that affects school or daily life if you go without it.

questions.q: 「想要」的东西都不应该买。
questions.qEN: You should never buy things you merely want.
questions.why: 想要的东西可以买。先保证需要，再在预算里给想要留一份。
questions.whyEN: Wants are fine. Cover needs first, then set aside part of the budget for wants.

questions.q: 突然很想买一件东西时，一个简单有效的办法是？
questions.qEN: You suddenly really want to buy something. A simple trick that works?
options: 马上下单，犹豫一下就会涨价
先加购物车，等一天再决定
问问主播还有没有别的优惠券
先借钱买下来，以后再慢慢还
optionsEN: Order now before the price goes up
Add it to the cart, decide tomorrow
Ask the streamer for another coupon
Borrow for it now and repay slowly
questions.why: 冷静期能过滤掉很多冲动。一天后还想要，再看预算。
questions.whyEN: A cooling-off period filters out a lot of impulses. Still want it tomorrow? Check the budget.

questions.q: 同学都有的东西，就是我的「需要」。
questions.qEN: If everyone in class has it, it's a need for me.
questions.why: 跟风带来的是「想要」。问问自己：没有它，生活和学习会不会真受影响？
questions.whyEN: Keeping up with others is a want. Ask: would life or school actually suffer without it?

questions.q: 旧手机还能正常用，新款一出就换，这属于？
questions.qEN: Your phone works fine, but you upgrade as soon as a new model drops. That's a…
options: 需要
想要
optionsEN: Need
Want
questions.why: 能用却想换，是想要。想要不是错，只是要知道自己在为什么花钱。
questions.whyEN: Replacing something that still works is a want. Not wrong, just know what you're paying for.

questions.q: 一件 199 元的衣服，一年只穿了 4 次，平均每次穿要花多少元？
questions.qEN: A ¥199 top you wore 4 times this year. What did each wear cost?
questions.why: 199 ÷ 4 ≈ 50 元。算「每次使用成本」，能帮你判断值不值。
questions.whyEN: 199 ÷ 4 ≈ 50. Cost per use is a quick way to judge whether something was worth it.

questions.q: 判断需要还是想要，最好的一个问题是？
questions.qEN: The best single question for telling a need from a want?
options: 它的价格是不是超出了预算
没有它，会不会影响生活学习
身边的同学是不是都已经有了
它是不是今年最流行的款式
optionsEN: Is it over my budget?
Would life or school suffer without it?
Do all my classmates already have it?
Is it this year's trendiest style?
questions.why: 价格、别人、颜值都不决定需不需要，影响才决定。
questions.whyEN: Price, other people and looks don't decide it. Impact does.

questions.q: 同一样东西，对一个人是需要，对另一个人可能只是想要。
questions.qEN: The same item can be a need for one person and a want for another.
questions.why: 学画画的同学需要好一点的颜料，对别人可能只是想要。判断要看自己的真实情况。
questions.whyEN: Good paints are a need for an art student and a want for most others. It depends on your situation.

questions.q: 陌生人介绍「刷单返利」：先垫钱，再返佣金。这是正规兼职。
questions.qEN: A stranger offers "order-boosting" work: pay upfront, get commission back. It's a real job.
questions.why: 刷单本身违规，「先垫付后返利」是最常见的诈骗套路：先小额返利让你信任，再让你越垫越多。
questions.whyEN: Order-boosting breaks the rules, and "pay first, get paid back" is the most common scam: small payouts build trust, then the amounts grow.

questions.q: 有人说「免费送游戏皮肤」，要你把手机收到的验证码告诉他。你应该？
questions.qEN: Someone offers a free game skin if you tell them the code texted to your phone. You…
options: 告诉他，反正皮肤是免费的
不给，验证码谁问都不给
只告诉他前面几位数字
让同学先去试试看
optionsEN: Tell them, the skin is free anyway
Refuse. Never share a code with anyone
Only tell them the first few digits
Let a friend try it first
questions.why: 验证码就是你账号的钥匙，谁要都不给，包括自称客服、老师、家人的人。
questions.whyEN: A verification code is the key to your account. Never share it, even with someone claiming to be support, a teacher or family.

questions.q: 全国统一的反诈预警劝阻专线是？
questions.qEN: China's national anti-fraud warning hotline is…
questions.why: 96110 是反诈预警劝阻专线，接到它的来电一定要接。12315 是消费投诉。
questions.whyEN: 96110 is the anti-fraud warning line. If it calls you, pick up. 12315 is for consumer complaints.

questions.q: 自称「公安局」的人打电话说你涉嫌犯罪，要你把钱转到「安全账户」。
questions.qEN: A caller says he's from the police, you're under investigation, and you must move money to a "safe account".
questions.why: 公检法不会通过电话办案，更没有「安全账户」。挂断，打 110 核实。
questions.whyEN: Police never handle cases by phone, and there's no such thing as a "safe account". Hang up and call 110.

questions.q: 有人低价卖游戏账号，要你「私下转账，别走平台」。最大的风险是？
questions.qEN: Someone sells a game account cheap but wants a private transfer, off the platform. The biggest risk?
options: 价格太便宜，可能收到的是次品
付完钱，对方可能直接拉黑你
账号等级太高，自己根本用不上
需要做实名认证，流程比较麻烦
optionsEN: It's so cheap it might be junk
Once you pay, they can just block you
The level's too high for you to use
It needs ID checks, which is a hassle
questions.why: 绕开平台就没有保障，这是游戏交易诈骗最常见的一步。
questions.whyEN: Leaving the platform removes every protection. It's the classic move in game-trade scams.

questions.q: 「退款链接」要你填银行卡号和密码，只要页面看起来像官方的就可以填。
questions.qEN: A refund link asks for your card number and PIN. If the page looks official, it's fine.
questions.why: 钓鱼网站可以做得和官方一模一样。退款只在官方 App 里操作，不点陌生链接。
questions.whyEN: Phishing pages can look identical to the real thing. Only handle refunds inside the official app.

questions.q: 以下哪句话最像骗子会说的？
questions.qEN: Which line sounds most like a scammer?
options: 「请在官方 App 内查看订单」
「就差你一个了，先别告诉家长」
「如有疑问请拨打官方客服」
「请勿向他人透露验证码」
optionsEN: "Please check your order in the official app"
"We only need you. Don't tell your parents yet"
"If in doubt, call official support"
"Never share your verification code"
questions.why: 制造紧迫、让你瞒着家人，是诈骗最典型的信号。
questions.whyEN: Urgency plus "keep it secret from your family" is the clearest scam signal there is.

questions.q: 不小心被骗转账后，应该马上报警（110），并保存聊天记录和转账凭证。
questions.qEN: If you've been tricked into sending money, call 110 right away and keep the chats and receipts.
questions.why: 越早报警，追回的机会越大。截图和转账记录是关键证据。
questions.whyEN: The sooner you report it, the better the chance of recovery. Screenshots and receipts are key evidence.

questions.q: 「0 利息」分期，但每期收 0.6% 手续费。这意味着？
questions.qEN: "Zero interest" instalments, but a 0.6% fee each month. That means…
options: 真的一分钱都不用多付给商家
手续费就是利息，实际更贵
只有第一期需要收取手续费
手续费等全部还完后会退回
optionsEN: You really pay the shop nothing extra
The fee is interest, it costs more
Only the first month has a fee
The fees come back once you finish
questions.why: 手续费按全部本金收，可你每月都在还本金。12 期算下来，实际年化成本约 13%。
questions.whyEN: The fee is charged on the full amount even as you pay it down. Over 12 months that's roughly 13% a year.

questions.q: 一部 3600 元的手机，分 12 期、每期 330 元，总共要付多少元？
questions.qEN: A ¥3,600 phone on 12 payments of ¥330. What do you pay in total?
questions.whyEN: 330 × 12 = 3,960. That's ¥360 more than paying upfront.

questions.q: 信用卡选「最低还款」后，没还的部分不会产生利息。
questions.qEN: After a credit card "minimum payment", the unpaid part doesn't collect interest.
questions.why: 没还的部分会按日计息，常见日利率万分之五，一年约 18%。
questions.whyEN: The unpaid balance accrues daily interest, commonly 0.05% a day, about 18% a year.

questions.q: 借 1000 元，一年后还 1100 元，年利率是多少？
questions.qEN: Borrow ¥1,000, repay ¥1,100 a year later. What's the annual rate?
questions.whyEN: The extra ¥100 is the interest. 100 ÷ 1,000 = 10%.

questions.q: 「先用后付」本质上也是一种借钱。
questions.qEN: "Buy now, pay later" is really a form of borrowing.
questions.why: 东西先拿到、钱以后给，就是借了一笔钱。逾期还会产生费用、影响信用。
questions.whyEN: Getting the item now and paying later is a loan. Late payment brings fees and can hurt your credit.

questions.q: 以下哪种情况，分期最可能是合理的？
questions.qEN: When is paying in instalments most likely reasonable?
options: 为了买最新款手机，在同学面前有面子
急需的学习用品，还得起、总价算清了
直播间限时优惠，不分期就抢不到
已经有几笔分期，再加一笔也差不多
optionsEN: The newest phone, to look good at school
A needed school item, affordable, total cost known
A livestream flash deal you'd miss otherwise
You already have a few, one more won't matter
questions.why: 分期不是不能用：真需要、还得起、算清总成本，三条都满足才考虑。
questions.whyEN: Instalments can be OK only if it's a real need, you can repay, and you know the full cost.

questions.q: 存 1000 元，年利率 2%，一年后大约有多少元利息？
questions.qEN: ¥1,000 saved at 2% a year. About how much interest after one year?
questions.why: 1000 × 2% = 20 元。对比一下：借钱的利率往往高得多。
questions.whyEN: 1,000 × 2% = 20. Compare that with borrowing rates, which are usually far higher.

questions.q: 网贷广告说「无抵押、秒到账」，说明它的利息一定很低。
questions.qEN: A loan ad says "no collateral, instant cash", so the interest must be low.
questions.why: 放款越容易，往往成本越高、风险越大。正规平台不向未成年人放贷。
questions.whyEN: The easier the money, the higher the cost usually is. Licensed lenders don't lend to minors.

questions.q: 「复利」的意思是？
questions.qEN: What does compound interest mean?
options: 利息只按本金算
利息也会再生利息
利率每年都翻倍
银行额外给的奖励
optionsEN: Interest only on the original amount
Interest earns more interest
The rate doubles every year
An extra bonus from the bank
questions.why: 利息加进本金，下一期连它一起算利息。时间越长，差别越大。
questions.whyEN: Interest is added to the balance, so next time it earns interest too. The longer, the bigger the gap.

questions.q: 每月存 100 元，坚持 3 年（不算利息），一共能存多少元？
questions.qEN: Save ¥100 a month for 3 years, ignoring interest. How much in total?
questions.why: 100 × 36 个月 = 3600 元。每月一点点，三年就是一大笔。
questions.whyEN: 100 × 36 months = 3,600. A little each month becomes a lot in three years.

questions.q: 攒钱越早开始越好，哪怕每次只存一点。
questions.qEN: Starting to save early matters, even with small amounts.
questions.why: 时间是复利最重要的原料。早点养成习惯，比金额大小更要紧。
questions.whyEN: Time is compounding's key ingredient, and the habit matters more than the amount.

questions.q: 以下哪个攒钱目标写得最好？
questions.qEN: Which saving goal is written best?
options: 我要多存点钱，存得越多越好
12 周存 600 元，每周存 50
等以后零花钱多了再开始存
一直存到自己不想存了为止
optionsEN: Save more, the more the better
¥600 in 12 weeks, ¥50 a week
Start when I get more pocket money
Keep going until I don't feel like it
questions.why: 好目标要具体：多少钱、多久、每次存多少。
questions.whyEN: A good goal is specific: how much, by when, and how much each time.

questions.q: 把钱单独放进储蓄目标，会让你更不容易乱花。
questions.qEN: Keeping savings in a separate goal makes you less likely to spend them.
questions.why: 单独放的钱，不容易被当成可以随便花的钱；看得见的目标也让花钱前多想一步。
questions.whyEN: Money set aside stops feeling like spending money, and a visible goal makes you pause.

questions.q: 「72 法则」：年收益率 6%，钱大约多少年能翻一倍？
questions.qEN: The Rule of 72: at 6% a year, roughly how many years for money to double?
questions.why: 72 ÷ 6 = 12 年。这是估算复利翻倍时间的小工具。
questions.whyEN: 72 ÷ 6 = 12 years. A quick way to estimate doubling time.

questions.q: 收到 2000 元压岁钱，最稳妥的第一步是？
questions.qEN: You get ¥2,000 in New Year money. The safest first step?
options: 全部买成游戏点卡，一次用完
和家长商量，存一部分花一部分
借给网上认识的朋友赚点利息
投进一个「稳赚不赔」的项目
optionsEN: Spend it all on game credits at once
Talk with your parents: save some, spend some
Lend it to an online friend for interest
Put it in a "can't-lose" scheme
questions.why: 存一部分、花一部分是好开始。「稳赚不赔」本身就是危险信号。
questions.whyEN: Saving some and spending some is a good start. "Can't lose" is itself a warning sign.

questions.q: 「稳赚不赔、高收益」的投资项目，值得马上投。
questions.qEN: A "guaranteed high return, zero risk" investment is worth jumping into.
questions.why: 收益和风险是绑在一起的。承诺高收益又没风险的，往往是骗局。
questions.whyEN: Return and risk come together. High return with no risk is usually a scam.

questions.q: 直播间喊「只剩最后 3 件，倒计时 10 秒」，主要是在利用什么？
questions.qEN: A livestream shouts "Only 3 left, 10 seconds!" What is it playing on?
options: 你对这件商品的真实需要
紧迫感，让你来不及思考
商品本身的质量很好
物流发货的速度很快
optionsEN: Your real need for the product
Urgency, so you don't stop to think
The product's great quality
Really fast delivery
questions.why: 倒计时和「最后几件」是为了让你跳过思考。慢下来，本身就是省钱。
questions.whyEN: Countdowns and "last few" exist to make you skip thinking. Slowing down saves money.

questions.q: 盲盒抽到隐藏款的概率通常很低，越想集齐花得越多。
questions.qEN: Rare figures in blind boxes are usually very unlikely, and chasing a full set costs more and more.
questions.why: 盲盒靠的是「下一个也许就是」的心理，和抽卡一样，很难控制花多少。
questions.whyEN: Blind boxes run on "maybe the next one", just like gacha, which makes spending hard to control.

questions.q: 会员「首月 1 元」，最该留意的是？
questions.qEN: A membership is ¥1 for the first month. What should you watch for?
options: 1 元的价格到底划不划算
会不会自动续费、下个月恢复原价
会员专属的图标和皮肤好不好看
能不能把账号分享给朋友一起用
optionsEN: Whether ¥1 is really a good deal
Whether it auto-renews at full price
Whether the member badge looks good
Whether you can share it with friends
questions.why: 很多低价首月会自动续费。开通时就设个提醒，或者及时关掉。
questions.whyEN: Many cheap first months auto-renew. Set a reminder when you sign up, or turn it off in time.

questions.q: 满 300 减 50。你本来只想买 220 元的东西，为了凑单买到 300 元。你实际多花了多少元？
questions.qEN: "¥50 off ¥300." You meant to spend ¥220 but padded the cart to ¥300. How much extra did you pay?
questions.why: 不凑单付 220，凑单付 300 − 50 = 250，多花 30 元买了本来不需要的东西。
questions.whyEN: Without padding: ¥220. With it: 300 − 50 = 250. You paid ¥30 more for things you didn't need.

questions.q: 「原价 999，现价 199」说明一定很划算。
questions.qEN: "Was ¥999, now ¥199" means it's definitely a bargain.
questions.why: 「原价」可能是虚标的。划不划算看你需不需要、和别家比价，而不是看划掉的数字。
questions.whyEN: The "original" price may be made up. Judge by need and comparison, not the crossed-out number.

questions.q: 以下哪个是「沉没成本」陷阱？
questions.qEN: Which one is the sunk-cost trap?
options: 票都买了，再难看也硬撑着看完
买东西之前先比较三家的价格
用优惠券买本来就要买的东西
把用不到的闲置物品挂出去卖掉
optionsEN: You paid, so you sit through a bad movie
Comparing three shops before buying
Using a coupon on something you'd buy anyway
Listing things you don't use for sale
questions.why: 已经花掉的钱收不回来，不该绑住接下来的选择。
questions.whyEN: Money already spent is gone. It shouldn't decide what you do next.

questions.q: 未成年人没经家长同意的大额打赏，家长可以依法要求平台退还。
questions.qEN: If a minor tips a streamer a large sum without parental consent, parents can legally ask the platform for a refund.
questions.why: 法律规定，这类和年龄不相适应、没经同意的支出可以要求返还。但最好的办法是一开始就不打赏。
questions.whyEN: By law, such unapproved spending beyond a minor's age can be reclaimed. Better still, don't tip in the first place.

questions.q: 「先用后付」「0 元下单」最容易让人怎样？
questions.qEN: "Pay later" and "¥0 checkout" most easily make people…
options: 让人花钱时更谨慎
忘了自己已经花了钱
帮人省下更多钱
让人更愿意记账
optionsEN: Spend more carefully
Forget they've already spent money
Save more money
Track spending more
questions.why: 付款的那一下被推迟了，花钱的感觉也就没了，账却还在。
questions.whyEN: The moment of paying is pushed back, so the spending doesn't feel real. The bill is still there.
